definitions.explanation: The quality or outcome of something that has been made or done. Refers to how well something turned out.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}は{出来|でき}がいい。
{今回|こんかい}のテストは{出来|でき}が{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: I did poorly on this test.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}のぶどうは{天候|てんこう}に{恵|めぐ}まれて、{出来|でき}が{素晴|すば}らしい。
examples.english: This year's grapes had favorable weather and turned out wonderfully.

notes:
Derived from the verb {出来|でき}る (to be able to; to be made). As a noun, {出来|でき} refers specifically to how well something turned out.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{出来|でき}がいい (turned out well)
・{出来|でき}が{悪|わる}い (turned out poorly)
・{出来|でき}{栄|ば}え (quality of work, how something turned out)
・{出来不出来|できふでき} (hit or miss, variable quality)
